title: Formulating a linear equation in one variable to solve problems
summary: Define one unknown, translate relationships into expressions, solve a linear equation and interpret the answer in context.
objectives: Choose and define a useful variable with its unit.
Translate verbal relationships into algebraic expressions and one equation.
Solve, check and report a context-appropriate answer.

blocks.text: Begin by stating what the variable represents. Express every other unknown quantity in terms of that variable. Use the sentence describing a total, difference or equality to form one equation.
After solving, attach the correct unit and check the value against the original story. Reject values that are impossible in context, such as a negative number of people.

sections.title: Modelling a perimeter problem

prompt.text: The length of a rectangle is 3 cm more than twice its width. Its perimeter is 42 cm. Find its width.

content.text: Let the width be x cm, so the length is 2x + 3 cm.

sections.verification_note: The dimensions are 6 cm and 15 cm, and 2(6 + 15) = 42 cm.

prompt.text: Three identical folders and a S$2 pen cost S$17. What is the price of one folder in dollars?

feedback.text: If x is the folder price, 3x + 2 = 17, so 3x = 15 and x = 5.

blocks.text: Define the variable and unit, express related quantities, form one equality, solve it, and check that the result makes sense in the story.
